intro: Denver beat the defending champion Seahawks in overtime on Thursday night, and the Eagles will play Sunday without Jalen Hurts. Minnesota and San Francisco are 5-0, Kansas City is 4-0, and Miami, Tennessee and the Chargers are still looking for a first win. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Cardinals trade Marvin Harrison Jr. to Houston as the losing streak hits four
top.dek: Arizona dealt its receiver to the Texans as the Lions game began Sunday, and he was inactive while the deal was pending. The Cardinals then lost 45-21 to fall to 1-4. Coach Mike LaFleur said the effort was not good enough.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Jalen Hurts ruled out against Carolina with a superficial blood clot
top.dek: Hurts was on the report with a calf injury, and on Thursday the Eagles ruled him out for Sunday. The team does not yet know how many games he will miss. Philadelphia is 2-3 and has lost three straight, so Tanner McKee takes the start.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 17: Puka Nacua's catches, a Monday Night Football record
top.dek: Nacua finished with 138 yards and a touchdown on a career-high 24 targets against Buffalo. Matthew Stafford went 40 of 54 for 383 yards and three scores. The Rams still lost 37-34 in overtime.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Cowboys visit Lambeau on Sunday Night Football
top.dek: Dallas plays at Green Bay at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. The Packers come off a 31-7 win over Chicago, and the Cowboys just reshuffled their defense. Watch who is active on the Green Bay defensive line and at corner.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills survive Rams in OT, head to Vegas

stories.text: Allen wins his first overtime game as Bills outlast Rams 37-34
stories.summary: Buffalo beat Los Angeles on Monday night to move to 4-1. Josh Allen had lost his previous seven overtime games, playoffs included. Khalil Shakir's 57-yard catch set up the winning drive, and Tyler Bass finished it with a 45-yard field goal.

stories.text: DJ Moore and Ed Oliver sit out again, Spencer Brown returns
stories.summary: Receiver DJ Moore (shoulder) and defensive lineman Ed Oliver (knee) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Tackle Spencer Brown went from limited with a back issue on Wednesday to full on Thursday. Receivers Joshua Palmer and running back Ty Johnson were limited, and no game designations have been posted yet.

stories.text: James Cook runs for 111 yards and two scores, then fumbles in OT
stories.summary: Cook carried 25 times for 111 yards and two touchdowns against the Rams. He lost a fumble in overtime, but Buffalo got the ball back and won anyway. Allen added 121 rushing yards of his own.

stories.text: 239: Josh Allen leads all quarterbacks in rushing yards
stories.summary: Allen's 239 rushing yards top every quarterback in the league. Buffalo also averages 32.8 points per game, tied for the NFL lead, but has committed nine giveaways over its last three games, four of them by Allen.

stories.text: Bills visit the Raiders Sunday at 4:25 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo plays at Allegiant Stadium on a short week after Monday night. Watch how Maxx Crosby and the Raiders' pass rush handle Allen, and whether the Bills clean up the turnovers. Former Bill Taron Johnson faces his old team for the first time.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: Winless Dolphins stick with Willis through bye

stories.text: Hafley says Malik Willis stays the starter at 0-5
stories.summary: Head coach Jeff Hafley shot down any talk of switching to Kyle McCord after Sunday's 31-24 loss to Cincinnati. He said five games is enough to judge Willis, but that the whole team has to play better. Hafley did not rule out bigger changes while the staff reviews everything during the bye.

stories.text: Brents, Moore and Louis get the bye to heal
stories.summary: Cornerback JuJu Brents left the Bengals game in the fourth quarter with a stinger, and safety Michael Taaffe is dealing with a chest injury. Hafley said Trey Moore and Kyle Louis will not practice during the bye and would not predict their availability for the Jets game. Running back De'Von Achane is on injured reserve with a knee injury.

stories.text: Ollie Gordon II carries the run game with Achane out
stories.summary: Gordon ran for 88 yards and a touchdown against Cincinnati. He has been Miami's lead back since Achane went down. Hafley praised Gordon and the offensive line after the game.

stories.text: 849: Willis's passing yards through five games, with 2 TDs and 4 INTs
stories.summary: Willis completes 56.2 percent of his throws, and his passing numbers rank last among starting quarterbacks. His 186 rushing yards rank third among quarterbacks. Miami signed him to a three-year, $67.5 million deal to be the starter.

stories.text: Dolphins are on bye, then play at the Jets on Oct. 25
stories.summary: Miami has no game this Sunday. The first game after the bye is at the New York Jets on October 25, followed by a home game against New England on November 1. Watch for lineup changes and a faster start from a young roster.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Maye and Patriots roll, Jets next at Gillette

stories.text: Patriots hammer Raiders 45-17 behind five Drake Maye touchdowns
stories.summary: New England piled up a season-high 536 yards and handed Las Vegas its second straight loss. Maye threw four touchdown passes and ran for another without a turnover, his first clean game of the season. He is the first Patriots quarterback since Tom Brady in 2018 with back-to-back games of three or more touchdown passes.

stories.text: Gonzalez back to full, Carlton Davis and Prunty sit out
stories.summary: Cornerback Christian Gonzalez was upgraded to full participation Thursday after being limited earlier in the week. Cornerbacks Carlton Davis (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring) and tackle Cory Durden (illness) did not practice. A.J. Brown (ankle), Will Campbell (knee) and Morgan Moses (foot) were limited, and no game designations have been posted.

stories.text: Drake Maye: 374 yards, four TDs and a 150.9 rating vs. Las Vegas
stories.summary: Maye went 26 of 34 against the Raiders for his second career 300-yard game. He sits at 7,898 career passing yards and needs 102 to reach 8,000. DeMario Douglas caught two touchdowns in the win.

stories.text: 536: Total yards in New England's season-best offensive day
stories.summary: The Patriots gained 536 yards and scored 45 points against Las Vegas, both season highs. Maye has thrown at least three touchdown passes in back-to-back games. New England owns a top-five defense going into the Jets game.

stories.text: Jets visit Gillette Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: A win would put New England at 3-0 at home and 2-0 in the division. The Patriots have beaten the Jets three straight, including a 42-10 road win on December 28 in which Maye threw five touchdowns. Both defenses rank in the top ten.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets' pass rush powers win, Pats up next

stories.text: Jets beat Browns 17-12 on a late Braelon Allen touchdown
stories.summary: New York got to 2-3 with a win at MetLife Stadium. Allen rushed for 116 yards on 24 carries, his first 100-yard game, and scored the go-ahead 22-yard touchdown with about three minutes left. Will McDonald recovered a fumble late to seal it, and the Jets committed 12 penalties.

stories.text: Hall, Mitchell, Ossai and Parham miss practice
stories.summary: Running back Breece Hall (quad), receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) and lineman Dylan Parham (knee) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Tight end Kenyon Sadiq, in the concussion protocol, was limited both days, along with safety Dane Belton and receiver Omar Cooper Jr. Game designations have not been posted.

stories.text: Rookie David Bailey grabs three sacks, all on Deshaun Watson
stories.summary: The No. 2 overall pick is the first Jets rookie with three sacks in a game since Hugh Douglas in 1995. Bailey has five sacks through five games. The Jets sacked Watson eight times in all.

stories.text: 293: Yards per game allowed, fourth best in the NFL
stories.summary: The Jets also rank second in yards allowed per play at 4.62. Three of their first five opponents finished with fewer than 200 total yards. They sacked Cleveland eight times, and Drake Maye has thrown 8 touchdowns and 7 interceptions this season.

stories.text: Jets at Patriots Sunday at 1:00 PM ET on CBS
stories.summary: New York opens a two-game AFC East stretch in Foxborough, then hosts Miami on October 25. The Jets have lost three straight to New England. Minkah Fitzpatrick and Demario Davis say stopping Maye's deep passing game is the priority.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Huntley keeps Ravens atop the North

stories.text: Ravens rally past Falcons in overtime without Lamar Jackson
stories.summary: Baltimore beat Atlanta 30-23 in overtime on Sunday night to reach 4-1 and take sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Backup Tyler Huntley tied the game with a 7-yard touchdown pass to Devontez Walker late in regulation, then scored the winner on a 1-yard sneak in overtime. Kyle Hamilton picked off Tua Tagovailoa to end it.

stories.text: Jackson sits out Thursday practice as the injury list grows
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson did not practice Thursday with the ankle sprain that kept him out of the Atlanta game, and he is questionable for Sunday in Cleveland. Receiver Rashod Bateman (shoulder) and guard John Simpson (groin) also sat out. Zay Flowers (toe) and Mike Green (hamstring) were limited, while Mark Andrews and Trey Hendrickson practiced fully.

stories.text: Huntley delivers in relief of Jackson
stories.summary: Tyler Huntley completed 24 of 32 passes for 201 yards against Atlanta and finished his last 11 attempts with a completion. He led a 14-play, 68-yard overtime drive and ran in the winning sneak himself. Coach Jesse Minter said after the game the team has full faith in its backup.

stories.text: 208: Rushing yards against a top-ranked run defense
stories.summary: The Ravens ran for 208 yards on Atlanta, more than the Falcons had allowed over their previous three games combined. Derrick Henry carried 24 times for 102 yards, and Justice Hill added 73 yards on four carries, including a 47-yard run from fullback.

stories.text: At Cleveland on Sunday in the North opener
stories.summary: Baltimore visits the 3-2 Browns on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. It is the first AFC North game for the Ravens this season. Jackson's ankle is the story to watch through Friday's report.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals enter bye with a winning record

stories.text: Burrow's four touchdowns send Bengals into the bye at 3-2
stories.summary: Cincinnati beat Miami 31-24 on Oct. 11 to snap a two-game losing streak. Joe Burrow threw four touchdown passes to four different receivers, tying the third-highest total of his career. The Bengals have a Week 6 bye, then travel to Baltimore.

stories.text: Chase and Higgins both played through injuries in Miami
stories.summary: Ja'Marr Chase practiced in the concussion protocol during the week, was listed questionable, and then played and caught six passes for 77 yards. Tee Higgins returned from groin and neck injuries and had two catches for 22 yards. The bye gives both extra time before the trip to Baltimore.

stories.text: Chase keeps climbing the franchise lists
stories.summary: Chase caught a one-handed 45-yard touchdown in the third quarter against Miami. It was his 58th career touchdown catch, the most of any NFL player since 2021. He also moved past Isaac Curtis for third on the Bengals' all-time receiving yards list with 7,126.

stories.text: 22: Straight field goals for Evan McPherson
stories.summary: McPherson hit a 26-yarder against Miami for his 22nd consecutive made field goal, a Bengals record. He passed Shayne Graham, who made 21 in a row.

stories.text: On bye, then at Baltimore on Oct. 25
stories.summary: Cincinnati is off this weekend. The Bengals visit the Ravens in Week 7 on Sunday, Oct. 25, with a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on CBS listed by the team. After that they host Tennessee on Nov. 1.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns look to bounce back against Baltimore

stories.text: Browns drop Jets game in the rain and end a three-game win streak
stories.summary: Cleveland lost 17-12 at the Jets on Oct. 11 and fell to 3-2. The offense never found a rhythm and Deshaun Watson went down eight times. First-year coach Todd Monken now gets the AFC North-leading Ravens at home on Sunday.

stories.text: Browns hold out seven players from Thursday practice
stories.summary: Running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle), linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle), tackles Mason Graham (knee) and Mike Hall (ankle) and Kalia Davis (quad) did not practice Thursday. Monken has called Judkins day-to-day, and Schwesinger has a Grade 1 ankle sprain after playing every defensive snap this year. Graham, who has a sprained MCL, was described as having a decent shot to play.

stories.text: Quincy Williams forces three fumbles in the loss
stories.summary: Linebacker Quincy Williams forced three fumbles against the Jets. Schwesinger added a strip-sack of Geno Smith. The defense finished with four sacks and eight tackles for loss, but it was not enough for a team that managed 198 net yards.

stories.text: 8: Sacks allowed by the Browns line against the Jets
stories.summary: Watson was sacked eight times and hit 13 times in the loss, and he finished 15 of 33 for 155 yards with a 69.6 passer rating. Monken pointed to communication problems up front and missed assignments. Watson had been sacked twice in each game of the win streak.

stories.text: Home against first-place Baltimore on Sunday
stories.summary: The Browns host the 4-1 Ravens on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. A Baltimore win would give the Ravens a clear lead in the division. Watch whether the line cleans up its protection and whether the injured defensive tackles are back.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Steelers ride Warren and Rodgers to 3-2

stories.text: Steelers pull away from Colts 34-22 to move to 3-2
stories.summary: Pittsburgh never trailed in a 34-22 win over Indianapolis on Oct. 11. Aaron Rodgers threw three touchdown passes for the third straight game, and Jaylen Warren produced two long scores. The Steelers sit one game behind Baltimore in the AFC North.

stories.text: Ramsey back at practice, Watt and Heyward full
stories.summary: Cornerback Jalen Ramsey (wrist) returned to limited work Thursday after missing Wednesday. T.J. Watt, Cam Heyward and running back Rico Dowdle moved to full participation, and Keeanu Benton (ankle) went from out to limited. Receivers Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) missed a second straight day.

stories.text: Warren scores from 80 and 50 yards against Indianapolis
stories.summary: Jaylen Warren gained 188 yards from scrimmage: 101 rushing, plus an 80-yard touchdown catch and a 50-yard touchdown run. He is the first player since Herschel Walker in 1986 to score on an 80-yard catch and a 50-yard run in the same game.

stories.text: 3: Straight games with three touchdown passes for Rodgers
stories.summary: Rodgers went 22 of 31 for 235 yards and three touchdowns against the Colts. The team says he is the first Steelers quarterback to throw for three scores in three consecutive games within one season. Only Terry Bradshaw and Ben Roethlisberger had done it at all in franchise history.

stories.text: At Tampa Bay on Sunday against a rookie quarterback
stories.summary: Pittsburgh visits the 1-4 Buccaneers on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Baker Mayfield is out with a thumb injury, so undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels is expected to make his third start. Tampa has the second-ranked run defense, which tests Warren.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans carry first win into London

stories.text: Texans finally get in the win column, 26-3 over Tennessee
stories.summary: Houston ended an 0-4 start by beating the Titans 26-3 in Week 5. The offense settled for four Ka'imi Fairbairn field goals in the first half, then got a Stroud rushing touchdown and a Stroud pass to Jaylin Noel after the break. The defense gave up three points, forced two turnovers and sacked Cam Ward four times.

stories.text: Montgomery and Pitre sit out again before London
stories.summary: Running back David Montgomery (groin) and safety Jalen Pitre (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, and both look likely to miss Sunday. Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (groin) and tackle Trent Brown (knee) went from no practice Wednesday to limited and full Thursday. Wide receiver Tank Dell took full reps but has not been activated from injured reserve.

stories.text: Stroud steady in the first win: 26 of 34 and no picks
stories.summary: C.J. Stroud completed 26 of 34 passes and scored twice, once through the air and once on the ground, against Tennessee. The offense sputtered early and stalled in the first half, and the Texans still piled up 11 penalties. Stroud has thrown six touchdown passes with no interceptions this season.

stories.text: 4: Fairbairn field goals before Houston scored a touchdown
stories.summary: All of Houston's first-half points against Tennessee came from kicker Ka'imi Fairbairn, who hit four field goals. The Texans led 12-3 at the break and added two touchdowns after halftime. A Brevin Jordan holding call also wiped out a Woody Marks touchdown run.

stories.text: Texans take on the Jaguars at Wembley
stories.summary: Houston plays at Jacksonville on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 9:30 a.m. ET from Wembley Stadium in London. NFL.com lists the broadcast on NFL Network and ESPN. Watch whether the Texans pass rush, led by Danielle Hunter and Will Anderson Jr., can pressure Trevor Lawrence behind a Jaguars line missing its left tackle.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts look to fix red zone against Titans

stories.text: Colts stall in the red zone and fall to Pittsburgh 34-22
stories.summary: Indianapolis dropped to 2-3 after losing at Pittsburgh. The Colts scored one touchdown on their trips inside the Steelers' 25 and gave up an 80-yard and a 50-yard score to Jaylen Warren. The next game is at home against winless Tennessee.

stories.text: Carlies and Dulin look doubtful to play Sunday
stories.summary: Linebacker Jaylon Carlies (ribs) and receiver Ashton Dulin (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, and the Colts could be without both against Tennessee. Tackle Jalen Travis (ankle) was limited Thursday after sitting out Wednesday. Daniel Jones (ankle) and Jonathan Taylor (rest) were full participants Thursday.

stories.text: Shrader keeps drilling long field goals
stories.summary: Kicker Spencer Shrader connected from 57 and 56 yards in the first half at Pittsburgh. His four makes from 55 or more yards with the Colts are the most in franchise history. The kicks also reflect a drive problem, since several Colts possessions ended in field goals instead of touchdowns.

stories.text: 3.0: Jonathan Taylor's yards per carry against Pittsburgh
stories.summary: Taylor ran 15 times for 45 yards, and one 20-yard carry made up nearly half of that. His other 14 carries gained 25 yards. Colts coverage graded the run game poorly and called the loss a step backward for the defense, too.

stories.text: Winless Titans visit Lucas Oil Stadium
stories.summary: Tennessee is at Indianapolis on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX. The Colts need a clean game against an 0-5 team. Watch whether the offense turns drives into touchdowns and whether the run defense tightens up.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars lead South, lose left tackle

stories.text: Jaguars beat Eagles 19-17 on a 57-yard Little kick
stories.summary: Cam Little hit a 57-yard field goal as time expired in London to give Jacksonville a 19-17 win over Philadelphia. The kick came one play after Ameer Abdullah returned a kickoff 53 yards, and after Jake Elliott had put the Eagles ahead with eight seconds left. The Jaguars are 4-1 and lead the AFC South by two games.

stories.text: Anton Harrison goes to IR with a knee injury
stories.summary: The Jaguars placed left tackle Anton Harrison on injured reserve after a noncontact right knee injury against the Eagles. He is expected to have arthroscopic surgery and must miss at least four games, and the team has not said who starts in his place. Long snapper Ross Matiscik (shoulder) is unlikely to play, so Jacob Bobenmoyer was signed.

stories.text: Trevor Lawrence throws for 356 and two scores in London
stories.summary: Lawrence finished with 356 passing yards and two touchdowns in the win over Philadelphia. One of them was a scoring throw to Parker Washington that put Jacksonville up 16-14. Lawrence now faces a Houston pass rush without his starting left tackle.

stories.text: 408-232: Jaguars outgained the Eagles and barely won
stories.summary: Jacksonville held a 408-232 yardage edge over Philadelphia. The Jaguars also failed to score a touchdown on three trips inside the Eagles' 20, including two at the 1-yard line, and went 2 of 4 on fourth down. That is why a game they controlled came down to the final kick.

stories.text: Jaguars host Texans at Wembley in first division game
stories.summary: Jacksonville faces Houston on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 9:30 a.m. ET at Wembley Stadium in London, its second straight game overseas. NFL.com lists the broadcast on NFL Network and ESPN. Four of the last five meetings were close, and this is the Jaguars' first AFC South game of the year.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Winless Titans look for answers at Indy

stories.text: Titans fall to 0-5 after a 26-3 loss in Houston
stories.summary: Tennessee scored only a short first-drive field goal against the Texans. Cam Ward went 23 of 36 for 170 yards, took four sacks and threw an interception. Calls to bench Ward are growing in the media, though no coach or team statement has said Tennessee will make a change.

stories.text: Hooker in concussion protocol, Spears limited
stories.summary: Safety Amani Hooker (concussion) and running back Tyjae Spears (knee) were limited Wednesday. Linebacker Kevin Winston Jr. (quad) did not practice, and Tony Pollard and John Franklin-Myers sat out for rest. Cornerback Joshua Williams practiced fully with a quad injury while on the return-to-practice window.

stories.text: Carnell Tate leads all rookies with 23 catches
stories.summary: The rookie receiver has 273 yards, second among rookies. He caught nine passes for 145 yards against Baltimore in Week 4, then managed one catch for six yards against Houston. Tate says he is focused on doing his own job.

stories.text: 3.2: yards per carry for a Titans run game that cannot move
stories.summary: Tennessee averaged 3.2 yards per rushing attempt against Houston, and the ground game has struggled all season. The offense also went three-and-out twice and turned the ball over twice. The Titans have scored three points in their last game.

stories.text: Titans try to find a first win at Indianapolis
stories.summary: Tennessee plays at the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1:00 p.m. ET on FOX at Lucas Oil Stadium. Watch the quarterback and whether the offense can run the ball. The Titans are looking for their first win of the season.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Defense wins it in overtime again

stories.text: Broncos survive the defending champs 17-14 in overtime
stories.summary: Denver built a 14-3 lead, watched Seattle erase it, then won on Wil Lutz's 53-yard field goal in overtime. The defense piled up five sacks, 17 quarterback hits and three takeaways. The Broncos are 4-2 and 3-0 at home.

stories.text: Surtain and Hufanga sit out; Moss returns to the lineup
stories.summary: Cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle, hurt Oct. 4 at San Francisco) missed his second straight game. Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) left the Chargers game last Sunday and was ruled out for Seattle. Cornerback Riley Moss was questionable after a limited practice week. No return dates have been given for Surtain or Hufanga.

stories.text: McMillian's interception sets up the winning kick
stories.summary: Ja'Quan McMillian picked off Sam Darnold in overtime, and four plays later Wil Lutz won it from 53 yards. Linebacker Alex Singleton led the defense with 13 tackles. Denver played without Patrick Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga and still sacked Darnold five times.

stories.text: 107: Bo Nix's passing yards in the win
stories.summary: Denver won with fewer than 175 passing yards for the first time since 1983. The Broncos were outgained 353 to 168 by Seattle. Both of their touchdown drives came in the first half, and they were shut out after the break.

stories.text: Broncos head to Arizona on Oct. 25
stories.summary: Denver has no game this Sunday. Next up is a trip to face the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 2:05 p.m. MT (4:05 p.m. ET) on CBS. The offense is the question after Thursday, and the secondary's health is the other one to watch.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Unbeaten Chiefs return from the bye

stories.text: Chiefs, the AFC's last unbeaten team, come off the bye
stories.summary: Kansas City sits at 4-0 and hosts the winless Chargers on Sunday. Mahomes said the early bye gave his surgically repaired knee an extra week of rest. A tough road run follows: Seattle, Denver, Buffalo, the Rams and Cincinnati.

stories.text: Rice misses another practice; rookie Woods added
stories.summary: Receiver Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday and is on track to miss the game. Left tackle Josh Simmons (back) and cornerback L'Jarius Sneed (knee) were limited both days. Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods (neck) joined the report Thursday as limited. Mahomes (knee) practiced fully.

stories.text: Mahomes posts his best passer rating since 2020
stories.summary: Four games back from a torn ACL, Mahomes has 1,037 passing yards, nine touchdowns and two interceptions. His 106.2 passer rating is the highest he has recorded since 2020. He called the bye a chance to take stock of his first few games.

stories.text: 5-0: a start Kansas City has made five times before
stories.summary: Kansas City has opened 5-0 five times before: 2003, 2013, 2017, 2018 and 2024. A win over the Chargers would make it six. The Chiefs have won seven of their last nine meetings with Los Angeles.

stories.text: Chargers visit Arrowhead on Sunday at 4:25
stories.summary: Kansas City hosts Los Angeles on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. The Chargers won the last two meetings, including a 16-13 game last season in which their defense shut out the Chiefs in the second half. Watch the injury report for Rice and Woods.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Cousins stays the starter for now

stories.text: Kubiak says Cousins is still the Raiders' QB
stories.summary: Rookie Fernando Mendoza made his NFL debut in garbage time of the loss to New England, which stirred talk of a switch. Coach Klint Kubiak ended that Monday and said Mendoza will be ready if needed. The Raiders started 3-0 and have lost two straight.

stories.text: Hemingway out of practice with a concussion
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (concussion) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, which points to him missing Sunday. Receiver Jalen Nailor (concussion) went from out of practice to limited. Tight end Brock Bowers (knee) moved from limited to full, and running back Ashton Jeanty (foot) practiced fully both days.

stories.text: Laube leads the league in kick return average
stories.summary: Dylan Laube averages 30.3 yards per kick return through five games, best in the NFL among players with at least 10 returns.

stories.text: 45-17: the Patriots' margin over Las Vegas in Week 5
stories.summary: New England's blowout was the Raiders' second straight loss after a 3-0 start. They dropped the Week 4 game to Kansas City by three points. Kirk Cousins has 1,269 yards and 12 touchdowns through five games.

stories.text: Bills visit Allegiant Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts Buffalo on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. Offensive coordinator Andrew Janocko is focused on getting the run game going against a strong Bills defensive line. Defensive coordinator Rob Leonard said his unit has to be better.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Winless Chargers face unbeaten Chiefs

stories.text: Harbaugh 'hellbent' on fixing an 0-5 start
stories.summary: The Chargers lost 23-17 to Denver in Week 5 and are 0-5 for the first time since 2003. Jim Harbaugh told players and the front office to keep fighting with a dozen games left. Los Angeles now visits unbeaten Kansas City.

stories.text: Alt, James and Harris sit out Wednesday practice
stories.summary: Left tackle Joe Alt (neck), safety Derwin James Jr. (hamstring) and receiver Tre' Harris (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday. Ladd McConkey (foot), Quentin Johnston (chest), Brenen Thompson (quad) and Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) were limited. Nearly 40 percent of the active roster was listed.

stories.text: Herbert takes five sacks and turns it over again
stories.summary: Justin Herbert went 14 of 24 for 121 yards with a touchdown and an interception against Denver. He was sacked five times and lost a fumble in the fourth quarter. He has nine turnovers through five games, and Harbaugh said he will not ask Herbert to change his style.

stories.text: 5: straight Chargers-Chiefs games decided by one possession
stories.summary: Each of the last five meetings has come down to one score. The Chargers won the last two, including 16-13 in Kansas City late last season. Derwin James Jr. sealed that game with an interception in the final minute.

stories.text: At Kansas City on Sunday, 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Chargers play at Arrowhead on Sunday, Oct. 18, with Kevin Harlan and Trent Green on the call. It is the first of two meetings with the Chiefs this season. Watch James's hamstring and the left tackle spot, since Alt is dealing with a neck injury.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys reshuffle the defense before Lambeau

stories.text: Cowboys shake up the defense after worst loss under Schottenheimer
stories.summary: Dallas dropped a 24-16 decision to a Tampa Bay team that had not won yet, and the fallout has reached the defensive staff. Christian Parker will call plays from the booth instead of the sideline, and Mike Pettine joins as a senior defensive advisor. The Cowboys now travel to Lambeau Field with a defense that ranks 31st in yards allowed.

stories.text: Overshown and Speed move up to limited, Durant still out
stories.summary: Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) and cornerback Ameer Speed (knee) were limited Thursday after sitting out Wednesday. Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) and Von Miller (rest) went full. Cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) missed a second straight day, so his chances against Green Bay look slim.

stories.text: Javonte Williams carries the Dallas ground game
stories.summary: Williams leads the Cowboys with 276 rushing yards, 18th among NFL backs. He scored three rushing touchdowns in the Week 4 win over Houston. The team as a whole averages 81.6 rushing yards per game, 30th in the league, so the load on him is heavy.

stories.text: 168.4: rushing yards per game Dallas allows, worst in the NFL
stories.summary: The Cowboys give up 168.4 rushing yards a game, the highest figure in the league, and rank 31st in total yards allowed. They also have three takeaways, tied for the fewest, and are the only team without an interception. Rashan Gary has 15 pressures but a 46.9 run defense grade from Pro Football Focus.

stories.text: At Green Bay, Sunday night at Lambeau Field
stories.summary: Dallas plays at the Packers on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. Dak Prescott has 1,381 passing yards and nine touchdowns through five games. Watch whether the Cowboys can slow Jordan Love, who threw for 367 yards against Chicago last week.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants erase 14 points to tie Washington

stories.text: Giants rally from 14 down to force overtime and tie Washington
stories.summary: New York trailed 27-13 with 11:05 left and tied it at 27 when Jameis Winston found Malik Nabers for a 17-yard touchdown with 1:43 to go. Neither team scored in overtime. It was the third straight Giants game decided in the final seconds, and it left them 3-1-1.

stories.text: Thomas, Eluemunor and Carter all sat out again Thursday
stories.summary: Left tackle Andrew Thomas (groin), right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf) did not practice for a second day. Cornerback Colton Hood (concussion) and safety Tyler Nubin (neck) also sat out. John Harbaugh called the main injured players day-to-day, and Marcus Mbow and J.C. Davis are the next tackles up.

stories.text: Dru Phillips piles up two sacks from the slot
stories.summary: The slot corner had two sacks, five solo tackles and four quarterback hits against Washington. He is the first Giants cornerback with two sacks in a game since 1996. He now leads all slot corners with six pressures this season.

stories.text: 33: Isaiah Likely's catches, a franchise tight end mark through five games
stories.summary: Likely leads the Giants with 33 receptions, the most by a Giants tight end through five games. He caught 11 of 13 targets for 94 yards and two touchdowns in the tie with Washington. He needs 10 more catches, 194 yards and three touchdowns to set career highs.

stories.text: Saints visit MetLife Stadium on Sunday
stories.summary: New York hosts New Orleans (1-4) on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Saints have lost three straight, and Harbaugh called them very hungry. Jameis Winston, who replaced the injured Jaxson Dart, starts again, and the Saints rank near the bottom in rushing yards allowed.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Hurts out with a blood clot, McKee starts

stories.text: Jalen Hurts ruled out against Carolina with a superficial blood clot
stories.summary: Hurts had been on the report with a calf injury, and on Thursday the Eagles ruled him out for Sunday because of a superficial blood clot. The team does not yet know how many games he will miss. The Eagles are 2-3 and have lost three straight.

stories.text: Barkley sits out all week, Smith returns to limited work
stories.summary: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) did not practice Thursday after missing Week 5. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) moved up to limited, while Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) and Jalyx Hunt (knee and ankle) did not practice. Landon Dickerson and three others opened practice windows after coming off injured reserve.

stories.text: Tanner McKee gets his first meaningful NFL start
stories.summary: McKee has started two games, both in Week 18 of the past two seasons, when Philadelphia had already clinched and rested its starters. Sunday is his first start with something at stake. The Eagles cut Andy Dalton last week, and the only other quarterback is fifth-round rookie Cole Payton.

stories.text: 31st: where the Eagles rank in yards per play
stories.summary: Philadelphia ranks 31st in yards per play and 31st in success rate on offense. It is 30th in EPA per play. The defense sits 17th in yards per play allowed.

stories.text: Panthers visit the Linc on Sunday at 1 p.m.
stories.summary: Philadelphia hosts Carolina (2-2, coming off a bye) on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Lincoln Financial Field. McKee starts at quarterback. Watch the backfield, where Barkley is in doubt.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Commanders still stinging from the clock fiasco

stories.text: Washington lets a win slip away on a clock management error
stories.summary: The Commanders led 27-13 in the fourth quarter, then tied the Giants in regulation. In overtime they reached field goal range with no timeouts, ran a play at 55 seconds, snapped again with 12 left and ran out of time before a kick. Dan Quinn said the late decisions left him gutted, and Jayden Daniels said the result was on him.

stories.text: Mariota, Diggs and Butler did not practice Thursday
stories.summary: Quarterback Marcus Mariota (knee), receiver Stefon Diggs (hamstring) and safety Percy Butler (hamstring) did not practice. Terry McLaurin (hamstring) and Austin Ekeler (chest) were limited. Game designations were not yet posted.

stories.text: Jayden Daniels runs for 103 yards and two scores
stories.summary: Daniels ran for 103 yards and two touchdowns against the Giants and threw for 199 yards on 17-of-25 passing. His 38-yard touchdown run hit 20.54 mph, the fastest speed of his career per Next Gen Stats.

stories.text: 95: second-half points allowed, the most in the NFL
stories.summary: Washington has allowed 95 points after halftime and 55 in the fourth quarter, both league highs. The defense ranks 32nd in opposing QBR in the fourth quarter and has no fourth-quarter sacks this season. The pattern showed again when New York scored 14 in the final minutes.

stories.text: At San Francisco on Monday Night Football
stories.summary: Washington plays the 5-0 49ers on Monday, Oct. 19, at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN at Levi's Stadium. Daniels faces San Francisco for the first time. Washington is 3-10-1 all time in regular-season games in San Francisco.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Williams trending toward a return at Atlanta

stories.text: Bears wait on Caleb Williams after a 31-7 loss in Green Bay
stories.summary: Chicago fell to 3-2 at Lambeau with Tyson Bagent starting for the second straight week. Coach Ben Johnson said Tuesday that Williams is progressing well from a Grade 2 hamstring strain suffered in Week 2, but he stopped short of confirming a return. The team will wait for medical clearance before it decides.

stories.text: Six Bears sat out Thursday practice, Williams went full
stories.summary: Linebackers T.J. Edwards and Keyshaun Elliott, defensive linemen Grady Jarrett and Dayo Odeyingbo, guard Joe Thuney and running back Kyle Monangai did not practice. Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson was limited. Williams and cornerback Kyler Gordon were full participants, and no game designations have been posted yet.

stories.text: Austin Booker finds the backfield in a lost game
stories.summary: Booker was one of the few Bears who stood out against Green Bay. He finished with two sacks, three tackles for loss, two quarterback hits and four solo tackles. His pass rush produced the only real disruption in a game the offense never controlled.

stories.text: 3.4: yards per carry the Bears managed against Green Bay
stories.summary: Chicago ran for 3.4 yards a carry against a run defense the Bleacher Nation recap called one of the league's worst. D'Andre Swift was the lone bright spot with 43 yards and a touchdown on nine carries. Bagent threw 12 of 21 for 87 yards and two interceptions before Case Keenum came in.

stories.text: Bears visit Falcons Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Chicago travels to Atlanta, which sits at 2-3 after a Week 5 loss. The first thing to watch is whether Williams starts. After that, watch whether the Bears can run the ball better than they did in Green Bay.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Gibbs sets touchdown mark as Lions hit the bye

stories.text: Gibbs passes Barry Sanders for the under-25 touchdown record
stories.summary: Jahmyr Gibbs scored his second touchdown against Arizona to reach 58 for his career, the most by any NFL player younger than 25. Sanders held the old mark at 57. Detroit won 45-21 and now rests on a bye at 3-2, tied with Green Bay and Chicago behind unbeaten Minnesota.

stories.text: White and Kennedy left the Arizona game hurt
stories.summary: Linebacker Devin White hurt his forearm and returner Tom Kennedy hurt his knee, and neither came back against the Cardinals. The bye gives both extra time before the Packers visit on Oct. 25. The Lions have not released a detailed update.

stories.text: Jameson Williams scores twice on two catches
stories.summary: Williams caught an 8-yard touchdown in the second quarter and a 39-yard touchdown in the third. He had two catches for 47 yards and both went for scores. Goff found him for the second one as Detroit pulled away from a 24-7 halftime lead.

stories.text: -9: Lions yards in the first quarter before a 45-point day
stories.summary: Detroit went three-and-out on its first three drives and trailed 7-0 after one quarter with negative nine total yards. The Lions then scored 31 straight points on the way to 45. It was also their first road win of the season.

stories.text: Lions are on a bye, then host Green Bay Oct. 25
stories.summary: Detroit has no game this weekend. The next one is Sunday, Oct. 25, at home against a Packers team that just beat Chicago 31-7. Use the week to watch how many starters get healthy.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers roll Bears, now host Cowboys on Sunday night

stories.text: Love and Watson carry Green Bay past Chicago 31-7
stories.summary: Jordan Love went 25 of 31 for 367 yards, the most by a Packers quarterback against the Bears at Lambeau. Green Bay forced five turnovers and moved over .500 for the first time this season at 3-2. Xavier McKinney intercepted Tyson Bagent twice.

stories.text: Four Packers did not practice Thursday
stories.summary: Defensive tackles Jonathan Ford (calf) and Javon Hargrave (Achilles), receiver Skyy Moore (ankle) and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring) sat out both Wednesday and Thursday. Cornerback Keisean Nixon (groin) was limited Thursday after sitting Wednesday. Receiver Savion Williams and tackle Jordon Riley were designated to return from injured reserve.

stories.text: Christian Watson turns two deep balls into scores
stories.summary: Watson caught six passes for 143 yards and two touchdowns against Chicago, both from Love. The scores covered 42 and 53 yards. Matthew Golden added six catches for a career-high 123 yards.

stories.text: 367: passing yards for Jordan Love against the Bears
stories.summary: No Packers quarterback had thrown for more against Chicago at Lambeau Field. Love completed 25 of 31 attempts with no turnovers listed in the recap. Both touchdown throws went to Watson.

stories.text: Cowboys visit Lambeau Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC
stories.summary: Green Bay hosts Dallas on Sunday Night Football at Lambeau Field. The injury report is long on the defensive line and at corner, so watch who is active. Hargrave and St-Juste both got hurt against Chicago.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Unbeaten Vikings use the bye to heal up

stories.text: Vikings go to 5-0 with a 23-13 win in New Orleans
stories.summary: Minnesota beat the Saints behind Justin Jefferson's return and a defense that gave up one offensive touchdown. The Vikings had entered allowing an NFL-low 12.8 points per game. They now take a Week 6 bye before hosting Indianapolis on Oct. 25.

stories.text: Bye week arrives with several Vikings banged up
stories.summary: Receiver Jordan Addison (hamstring) and running back Jordan Mason (thumb) are on the list, as are tight end T.J. Hockenson and tackle Christian Darrisaw (both concussion). Hockenson left the Saints game after the first pass play. The team hopes Mason can come off injured reserve for the Colts.

stories.text: Jefferson returns from ankle injury with a leaping touchdown
stories.summary: Justin Jefferson came back from a Week 4 ankle injury and caught six passes for 79 yards. His 15-yard touchdown from Kyler Murray came on a leaping catch. Aaron Jones added 113 rushing yards on 25 carries.

stories.text: 142: total yards the Vikings allowed to New Orleans
stories.summary: The Saints gained 142 yards and scored one offensive touchdown, a 2-yard run by Kendre Miller. Their other score came on an 87-yard fumble return. Byron Murphy Jr. intercepted Tyler Shough, who threw for 96 yards and two picks.

stories.text: Vikings are on a bye, then host the Colts Oct. 25
stories.summary: Minnesota has no game this weekend. The next one is Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET against Indianapolis at U.S. Bank Stadium. Watch the tight end and left tackle spots coming out of the bye.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons look to rebound after overtime heartbreak

stories.text: Falcons let a lead slip and lose in overtime to Baltimore
stories.summary: Atlanta led 14-9 at the half and 17-15 in the third quarter, then fell 30-23 in overtime to a Ravens team playing without Lamar Jackson. Tyler Huntley threw for 201 yards and two scores and ran in the winning sneak. The loss drops the Falcons to 2-3.

stories.text: Penix on track to start after rib injury
stories.summary: Michael Penix Jr. left the Ravens game late with a rib injury, but coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday he feels better and should start against the Bears barring a setback. Penix made every throw in practice. Cornerback C.J. Henderson (groin), who has filled in for injured reserve corner A.J. Terrell Jr., missed Wednesday but is not ruled out.

stories.text: Jessie Bates III scores and makes a late stop
stories.summary: Bates returned a fumble 36 yards for a first-quarter touchdown, the first score of his career. In the third quarter he knocked away a two-point try aimed at Mark Andrews, which kept Atlanta ahead 17-15 at that point.

stories.text: 200: Jake Matthews' consecutive starts, longest active streak in the NFL
stories.summary: The Falcons left tackle played through a groin injury Sunday night and made his 200th straight start. No active player in the league has a longer run.

stories.text: Bears visit Atlanta on Sunday
stories.summary: Atlanta hosts Chicago at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1 p.m. ET on Fox, per the team schedule. Watch Penix's rib and whether the secondary holds up without Terrell and possibly Henderson.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Young returns from the bye with Eagles up next

stories.text: Bryce Young says he is excited to be back after the bye
stories.summary: Young spent the bye week away from the team and said Tuesday he missed football and his teammates. Through four games he has 1,268 passing yards, nine touchdowns and two interceptions as Carolina sits at 2-2 heading to Philadelphia.

stories.text: Rookie tackle Monroe Freeling limited with a knee injury
stories.summary: Right tackle Monroe Freeling missed Wednesday and was limited Thursday. Running back A.J. Dillon (ankle) did not practice either day, and Jaelan Phillips (hamstring), Damien Lewis (elbow), Darren Waller (toe) and Tommy Tremble (ribs) were limited. If Freeling cannot go, Stone Forsythe is the likely starter. Cornerback Jaycee Horn remains on injured reserve with a torn quad.

stories.text: Tetairoa McMillan keeps producing for Carolina
stories.summary: McMillan caught 14 passes for 192 yards and two touchdowns against Detroit. For the season he has 26 catches for 385 yards and two scores, and he is the 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year.

stories.text: 9.0: Panthers' yards per attempt with Jalen Coker on the field
stories.summary: Carolina averages 9.0 yards per pass attempt with Coker in the game, which would rank second in the NFL. Without him that number drops to 6.5, which would rank 23rd. Coker left early in the third game and is likely to return Sunday.

stories.text: Panthers visit Eagles at the Linc on Sunday
stories.summary: Carolina plays at Philadelphia on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Panthers come off a bye at 2-2. Watch the right tackle spot and whether Coker is back in the lineup.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints search for an offense at 1-4

stories.text: Saints offense stalls in 23-13 loss to Minnesota
stories.summary: New Orleans managed 142 total yards against the Vikings, and Tyler Shough threw for 96 yards with two interceptions. The loss left the Saints at 1-4 and put coach Kellen Moore under pressure to fix the offense.

stories.text: Olave sits out with illness; Shough practices fully
stories.summary: Wide receiver Chris Olave did not practice Wednesday or Thursday with an illness, as did lineman Nathan Shepherd. Linebacker Kaden Elliss (calf) and edge Anfernee Jennings (knee) also sat out. Shough was a full participant with a left hand injury, and Alvin Kamara was limited with a back issue.

stories.text: Chris Olave climbs the Saints' career receptions list
stories.summary: Olave recently moved into second place on the franchise career receptions list, doing it in his first 60 games. His availability for Sunday depends on how he recovers from the illness that kept him off the practice field this week.

stories.text: 30.2: points per game the Saints allow, 31st in the NFL
stories.summary: New Orleans also ranks 30th against the run at 148.8 yards per game and sits at minus 6 in turnover margin. Those numbers explain a lot of the 1-4 start.

stories.text: Saints face the Giants at MetLife on Sunday
stories.summary: New Orleans visits the Giants (3-1-1) on Sunday, Oct. 18, at noon CT (1 p.m. ET) on Fox. The Saints have won the last three meetings in the series. Watch whether the run defense can slow New York.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs have a win and a quarterback question

stories.text: Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels gets Tampa Bay its first win
stories.summary: Daniels completed 19 of 25 passes for 189 yards and a touchdown in a 24-16 Thursday night win over Dallas, in only his second start. The win lifted the Bucs to 1-4 and kept them from an 0-5 start for the first time since 2013.

stories.text: Mayfield and Winfield still not practicing
stories.summary: Baker Mayfield (right thumb) and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib) did not participate Wednesday or Thursday. Sean Tucker (quad) moved up to limited, and Chris Godwin Jr. and Tristan Wirfs were full. Mayfield is not expected to play Sunday, which points to Daniels again.

stories.text: Bucky Irving runs for a career high against Dallas
stories.summary: Irving set a career best with 165 rushing yards and two total touchdowns, per NFL.com. He broke a 72-yard run in the third quarter and added a 22-yarder that helped seal the game.

stories.text: 214: rushing yards for Tampa Bay against Dallas
stories.summary: The Bucs ran for 214 yards, forced three takeaways and held the Cowboys to 16 points. That formula gave a rookie quarterback room to work.

stories.text: Steelers visit Raymond James on Sunday
stories.summary: Pittsburgh visits Tampa Bay on Sunday, Oct. 18, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. The Steelers lead the all-time series 10-2, and each of the last three meetings was decided by three points or fewer. Daniels could become the first undrafted rookie quarterback since Warren Moon in 1984 to beat Pittsburgh as a starter.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Harrison gone, losses piling up at 1-4

stories.text: Cardinals ship Marvin Harrison Jr. to Houston as the losing streak hits four
stories.summary: Arizona traded receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Texans as the Lions game began Sunday, and he sat out as inactive while the deal was pending. The Cardinals then lost 45-21 to fall to 1-4. Coach Mike LaFleur called the effort not good enough.

stories.text: Rookie back Jeremiyah Love sits out Wednesday with a bad ankle
stories.summary: Love did not practice Wednesday because of a left ankle injury he picked up in Week 4 against the Giants. He played through it against Detroit and carried 12 times for 22 yards. Safeties Wydett Williams (concussion) and Andrew Wingard (knee) also missed practice, and Kitan Crawford was limited as he works back from injured reserve.

stories.text: Brissett throws for 292 and three scores in a lost cause
stories.summary: Jacoby Brissett completed 29 of 47 passes for 292 yards and three touchdowns against Detroit, with one interception and five sacks taken. LaFleur said Brissett was not the problem and has not committed to a switch to rookie Carson Beck, though the staff will talk about it.

stories.text: 31: points or more allowed in each of Arizona's four losses
stories.summary: The Cardinals have given up at least 31 points in each of their four defeats. Detroit scored on seven straight possessions Sunday, six of them touchdowns, and Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 151 yards at 6.0 a carry.

stories.text: At the Rams on Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Arizona visits SoFi Stadium on Sunday, October 18 to face a Rams team that sits at 2-3. Watch whether Love can go and how a thin secondary handles Puka Nacua and Davante Adams.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams fall in a 37-34 overtime thriller

stories.text: Rams lose to Bills 37-34 in overtime on Monday night
stories.summary: Matthew Stafford drove 63 yards in 1:34 and Kyren Williams scored with five seconds left to tie it at 34. In overtime the Rams missed a 48-yard field goal that Buffalo blocked, and Tyler Bass won it from 45 yards. Los Angeles drops to 2-3.

stories.text: Tight end Davis Allen sits out with a foot injury
stories.summary: Allen did not practice Thursday after hurting his foot against Buffalo and could miss Sunday. Colby Parkinson (shoulder), Nate Landman (wrist and shoulder) and Josh Wallace (shoulder) were limited. Lineman Alaric Jackson is suspended for the game after throwing a punch at Bradley Chubb, and Myles Garrett is still on injured reserve.

stories.text: Puka Nacua catches 17 passes for 138 yards and a score
stories.summary: Nacua saw 24 targets against Buffalo, a career high, and his 17 catches set a Monday Night Football record. Stafford finished 40 of 54 for 383 yards and three touchdowns.

stories.text: 454: yards the Rams gained and still lost
stories.summary: Los Angeles outgained Buffalo 454 to 436, but the game turned on a blocked field goal in overtime. The teams combined for 890 yards, eight lead changes and 35 fourth-quarter points.

stories.text: Home against Arizona on Sunday, 4:05 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The Rams host the 1-4 Cardinals at SoFi Stadium on Sunday, October 18. Watch the tight end room, with Allen in doubt, and the kicking game after Buffalo blocked their overtime attempt.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers unbeaten and waiting on Bosa

stories.text: 49ers hold off Seattle 32-29 to stay unbeaten at 5-0
stories.summary: San Francisco won in Seattle behind two Brock Purdy touchdown passes and four takeaways. The Niners can start 6-0 for the first time since 2019 if they beat Washington on Monday night.

stories.text: Bosa, Juszczyk and Thompson all questionable for Monday
stories.summary: Nick Bosa has missed time with a calf injury since before Week 3. Kyle Juszczyk (knee) and James Thompson Jr. (ankle) are also questionable. Deebo Samuel will miss time with a hamstring injury, and Christian Kirk is not expected back for Washington.

stories.text: Mike Evans leads the way with 113 yards and a touchdown
stories.summary: Evans caught seven passes for 113 yards and a score in the win at Seattle. He enters Monday with 111 career touchdown catches, tied for ninth in NFL history with Tony Gonzalez.

stories.text: 23: quarterback pressures from a defense without Bosa
stories.summary: The 49ers rushed Seattle without Bosa and still recorded five sacks and 23 pressures. Renardo Green had two interceptions in the game.

stories.text: Washington on Monday, 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN/ABC
stories.summary: The 49ers host the Commanders (1-3-1) at Levi's Stadium on Monday, October 19. Watch Bosa's status and whether linebacker Dre Greenlaw's one-game suspension holds up on appeal.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Darnold's overtime pick sinks Seattle

stories.text: Darnold's overtime interception hands Denver a 17-14 win
stories.summary: Seattle erased a 14-3 deficit and tied the game on Jason Myers's 34-yard field goal with three seconds left. In overtime, Sam Darnold threw to Rashid Shaheed on third down and Ja'Quan McMillian intercepted it, and Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard winner. The Seahawks are 3-3.

stories.text: Charbonnet has a real chance to return in Week 7
stories.summary: Running back Zach Charbonnet, who tore his ACL in last season's divisional round, could make his season debut against Kansas City. First-round pick Jadarian Price is on injured reserve with a chest injury and cannot return before November 2.

stories.text: Emanuel Wilson carries the backfield with 251 yards in two games
stories.summary: With the top backs out, Wilson ran 73 times for 251 yards and two touchdowns over the past two weeks. Seattle used George Holani for a one-yard touchdown run in the comeback against Denver.

stories.text: 353: yards Seattle gained against 168 for Denver, and lost
stories.summary: The Seahawks outgained the Broncos by 185 yards but turned the ball over three times, including two Darnold interceptions. Darnold has thrown seven interceptions in four games, after 14 all of last season.

stories.text: Home against Kansas City on Sunday, October 25
stories.summary: Seattle played Thursday, so it has no game this Sunday. The Chiefs visit on October 25 in a Sunday night game on NBC, which is subject to flex scheduling, and Charbonnet's availability is the thing to watch.
